pushback_verification: This record exists because the GATE CAUGHT THE PREVIOUS ONE. The 07-54-34Z walk wrote 11 resolution entries for 11 findings and still failed clause (b): five of its titles were ABBREVIATED paraphrases of the reviewed findings rather than verbatim, so the completeness check — which matches on (title, file) — found five substantive findings unnamed and correctly reported the pass unresolved. The record looked complete by count and was incomplete by name. That is rc02's completeness-before-disposition clause operating as designed, on the walk of the change that is itself about not trusting what a record appears to say; without it the gate would have advanced on an under-named record. CORRECTION IS ADDITIVE: the earlier record is committed and stands unmodified on the trail, and this one supersedes it as the latest resolving record for the pass. No disposition, no lane, and no edit changed — every action string is carried over verbatim from the record it corrects. DISCIPLINE FOR THE FUTURE: a walk MUST echo each finding's title byte-for-byte; paraphrasing a title silently breaks the coverage check that makes clause (b) meaningful.

resolutions.action: VERIFIED FIRST: zero `orbit status` occurrences in review.ts:288-496 — the reviewer is right and the premise was false. The MODIFIED requirement now says the branch SHALL run `orbit status --change <name> --json` as an explicit step ordered BEFORE the cycle-context step, stating that no such call exists today. proposal.md's 'both read a slot they already have access to' rewritten; design.md D1 carries the correction inline; tasks.md 1.1 is now ADD the step rather than read an existing one.

resolutions.title: `next_hint_keys.slot` is ABSENT in two common current-engine states, so fail-closed withholds from exactly the sequential iterations D4 protects
resolutions.action: Settled by D-rc03a-7, ratified before the walk. Both delta specs carry a decision table whose absent-slot rows are stated by construction, naming both causes the reviewer found. design.md D3 was REPLACED and records why the original was reversed rather than defended: its consequence-asymmetry argument only holds if fail-closed misfires rarely, and it misfires on two routine states.

resolutions.title: The rule keys on the RECOMMENDED-NEXT slot, not on the class of the pass actually being run
resolutions.action: Same root cause as the absent-slot CRITICAL, fixed by the same conjunction: its second term is the INVOKED reviewer class. Both decision tables carry an explicit `blind-pair` + `in-context` row that RETAINS, with the reviewer's own reasoning recorded — an in-context pass can never satisfy a blind-pair slot and is, per rc03's charter, the verification genre that most needs prior context. Scenario added; task 2.5 added.

resolutions.title: The stated duplicate-findings cost understates it: a blinded re-report feeds the gate's convergence predicate and burns budget
resolutions.action: Named in both places. The requirement's deliberate-cost paragraph now states the mechanism the reviewer traced: a finding closed by a RATIFIED DECISION rather than an artifact edit leaves no current-state evidence for pushback, so a blinded member can re-report it as live; the gate reads a pass's IMMUTABLE severity counts, not the walk's suppressions, so the re-report fails the confirm predicate and buys a further independent pass against the declared budget. Recorded as ACCEPTED, not mitigated, with the reason: a deflated residual estimate is the worse failure because it is invisible, where a spent pass is not.

resolutions.title: R-crc-7 requires a decision procedure to be a DECISION TABLE, not prose plus a blanket default
resolutions.action: Both delta specs now specify the rule as a decision table rather than a prose paragraph, with the absent-slot rows explicit by construction and their causes named. The reviewer's causal claim is worth recording: the blanket fail-closed default is precisely how the two real absent-slot states went unstated, so the R-crc-7 violation and the CRITICAL it produced are the same defect at two levels.

R-crc-1's ceiling is counted in capabilities touched, so the charter line is the figure a sizing check would read.
